issues.legal_issue: An application to refer a dispute to arbitration is not required to be dismissed for initially omitting the arbitration agreement if the original agreement or a duly certified copy is on the record when the court considers the application.
material_facts: The defendants applied to refer the suit dispute to arbitration without attaching the retirement deed or partnership deed.
The plaintiffs had referred to and relied on those deeds in their suit and had filed photocopies of them.
The defendants produced the original deeds three days after filing their application, and the court had them before it when it decided the application.
issues.conclusion: The initial omission did not require dismissal of the application because the original deeds were on the record before the court considered it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 bars the court from considering an application under Section 8(1) unless the original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy is before it. The word “entertained” concerns consideration of the application on its merits, not merely its filing. The Court applied the reasoning on “entertained” in Hindusthan Commercial Bank Ltd. v. Punnu Sahu and Martin and Harris Ltd. v. VIth Additional District Judge, which discussed Lakshmiratan Engineering Works Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner. It distinguished Atul Singh v. Sunil Kumar Singh and noted Bharat Sewa Sansthan v. U.P. Electronics Corporation Ltd., but expressly left open whether photocopies already on the record, without more, satisfy Section 8(2).

predicates.arbitration_referral_application: A party to a court proceeding applies to have the dispute referred to arbitration.
predicates.agreement_on_record_when_considered: The original arbitration agreement or a duly certified copy is before the court when it considers the referral application.

issues.definition: When a party seeks referral to arbitration and the original agreement or a duly certified copy is before the court at consideration, an earlier omission to attach it does not require rejection of the application.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute may be referred to arbitration despite one named party to the suit not being a party to the arbitration agreement when the other material parties are bound by it and the non-signatory has no relevant right in the dispute.
material_facts: The plaintiffs were parties to the arbitration agreement or claimed through a person who was a party to it, and the relevant defendants were also parties or claimed through parties.
One defendant was not a party to either deed containing an arbitration clause.
On the plaintiffs’ own case, that defendant had inherited no right or share in the partnership or the scheduled property.
The suit dispute concerned benefits arising from the retirement deed and partnership deed, and the trial court found that referring it would not require bifurcation of the cause of action or parties.
issues.conclusion: The presence of the one defendant who was not party to the arbitration agreement did not prevent referral of the dispute between the parties to arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to the facts, the Court endorsed the trial court’s view that a non-signatory defendant’s presence did not prevent referral where the plaintiffs and the other material parties were parties to the arbitration agreement personally or through those from whom they claimed, the non-signatory had inherited no relevant right, and referral would not bifurcate the cause of action or parties. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: court_referral_application and dispute_arises_from_arbitration_agreement and material_parties_bound and non_signatory_lacks_relevant_right and no_bifurcation_needed

predicates.court_referral_application: A party asks a court to refer a civil dispute to arbitration.
predicates.dispute_arises_from_arbitration_agreemen: The dispute concerns rights or benefits arising from deeds containing an arbitration agreement.
predicates.material_parties_bound: The parties with relevant rights in the dispute are parties to the arbitration agreement or claim through someone who is a party.
predicates.non_signatory_lacks_relevant_right: A named party who did not agree to arbitration has no inherited or other relevant right in the dispute.
predicates.no_bifurcation_needed: Referring the dispute does not require separating the cause of action or the parties for adjudication.

issues.definition: If a court is asked to refer a dispute arising from an arbitration agreement, the material parties are bound by it, a non-signatory has no relevant right, and referral requires no bifurcation, that non-signatory’s presence does not bar referral.

issues.legal_issue: The unregistered status of a partnership does not prevent referral to arbitration of a dispute covered by an arbitration agreement in its deeds.
material_facts: The retirement deed and partnership deed contained arbitration clauses covering disputes connected with the deeds and partnership affairs.
The parties to the deeds, and those claiming through them, had agreed to resolve covered disputes by arbitration.
issues.conclusion: The partnership’s unregistered status did not prevent the dispute from being referred to arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no provision in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, or any other statute that prohibited referral to arbitration of a dispute concerning an unregistered partnership deed. It relied on the arbitration clauses and the agreement of the partners and persons claiming through them; it cited no earlier case on this issue.

predicates.arbitration_referral_proceeding: A party to a court proceeding seeks referral of a dispute to arbitration.
predicates.unregistered_partnership: The partnership connected with the dispute has not been registered.
predicates.applicable_arbitration_agreement: The relevant parties agreed to arbitrate disputes of the kind raised in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When referral is sought in a dispute concerning an unregistered partnership and an applicable arbitration agreement exists, the partnership’s unregistered status does not bar referral.
